calculators.title_native: Irish PAYE Income Tax, USC & PRSI Take-Home Pay Calculator
calculators.title_en: Irish PAYE Income Tax, USC & PRSI Take-Home Pay Calculator
search_terms_native: income tax calculator standard rate cut off
calculators.description_native: Calculate net monthly and annual take-home pay under Irish Revenue Commissioners rules, accounting for PAYE Income Tax bands (20%/40%), Universal Social Charge (USC), Class A PRSI, Personal & PAYE Tax Credits, Rent Tax Credit, and tax-relieved pension contributions.

inputs.name: age_group
inputs.label_native: Age Group (For Pension Relief Cap & USC Concessions)

calculators.formula_explanation:
1. Gross Taxable Pay: Sum of Gross Salary + Annual Benefit-in-Kind (BIK).
2. Pension Tax Relief: Age-based percentage cap applied to gross salary (up to an annual salary cap of €115,000): Under 30 (15%), 30-39 (20%), 40-49 (25%), 50-54 (30%), 55-59 (35%), 60+ (40%). Allowable pension deduction reduces income taxable for PAYE Income Tax at marginal rate.
3. Standard Rate Cut-Off Point (SRCOP): Single/Single Parent: €42,000; Married One Earner: €51,000; Married Two Earners: €84,000 combined (max €51,000 per spouse).
4. Gross PAYE Income Tax: 20% on taxable income up to SRCOP; 40% on portion exceeding SRCOP.
5. Tax Credits Deducted: Personal Tax Credit (€1,875/€2,000) + Employee PAYE Tax Credit (€1,875/€2,000) + Single Person Child Carer Credit (€1,750 if applicable) + Rent Tax Credit (€750 single / €1,500 married) + Other Credits. Net Income Tax = Max(0, Gross Income Tax - Total Tax Credits).
6. Universal Social Charge (USC): Calculated on Gross Salary + BIK (before pension deduction). Exempt if total gross earnings ≤ €13,000. Standard rates: 0.5% up to €12,012; 2% on €12,012.01 to €25,760; 4% on €25,760.01 to €70,044; 8% on excess above €70,044. (Concession rate of 2% max applies for Full Medical Card holders / Age 70+ earning ≤ €60,000).
7. Employee PRSI (Class A1): 4.1% on total gross income. Exemption if weekly gross earnings ≤ €352. Weekly earnings between €352.01 and €424 receive a tapered PRSI Credit (Maximum €12 per week reduced by 1/6th of earnings above €352).
8. Net Take-Home Pay = Gross Salary - Net Income Tax - USC - Employee PRSI - Employee Pension Contribution.

calculators.title_native: Irish Sole Trader & Self-Employed Tax Calculator (Class S PRSI, USC & Earned Income Credit)
calculators.title_en: Irish Sole Trader & Self-Employed Tax Calculator (Class S PRSI, USC & Earned Income Credit)
calculators.description_native: Calculate income tax, Class S PRSI, USC, and net earnings for self-employed individuals, sole traders, and umbrella company contractors in Ireland, including Preliminary Tax payment requirements and Earned Income Tax Credit.
calculators.formula_explanation:
1. Net Business Profit: Gross Revenue minus Allowable Operating Expenses.
2. Taxable Income for Income Tax: Net Business Profit minus Personal PRSA Pension Contribution (capped by age percentage up to €115,000 earnings limit).
3. Income Tax: 20% on taxable income up to Standard Rate Cut-Off Point (€42,000 single / €51,000 married single earner); 40% on balance above SRCOP.
4. Tax Credits: Personal Tax Credit (€1,875/€2,000) + Earned Income Tax Credit (€1,875/€2,000, which replaces PAYE Credit for self-employed individuals). Net Income Tax = Max(0, Gross Income Tax - Tax Credits).
5. Universal Social Charge (USC): Calculated on Net Business Profit. Standard bands (0.5%, 2%, 4%, 8%). Crucial Edge Case: Self-employed non-PAYE income exceeding €100,000 is subject to a 3% USC surcharge (yielding an 11% marginal USC rate on portion over €100,000).
6. Class S PRSI: 4.1% of total Net Business Profit, subject to a statutory minimum payment of €500 per year. (No weekly earnings exemption or PRSI credit for Class S).
7. Total Tax Liability = Net Income Tax + USC + Class S PRSI.
8. Preliminary Tax Requirement: Payable by October 31 annually, calculated as 100% of previous year's tax liability or 90% of current year's estimated liability.
9. Net Retained Earnings = Net Business Profit - Total Tax Liability - Pension Contribution.

calculators.title_native: Irish Property Stamp Duty, Mortgage Borrowing & First-Time Buyer Scheme Calculator
calculators.title_en: Irish Property Stamp Duty, Mortgage Borrowing & First-Time Buyer Scheme Calculator
search_terms_native: help to buy scheme calculator ireland
mortgage lti calculator central bank ireland
calculators.description_native: Calculate residential Stamp Duty, Central Bank Loan-to-Income (LTI) borrowing limits, Help to Buy (HTB) tax refunds, First Home Scheme (FHS) equity support, and total upfront cash required for buying property in Ireland.

inputs.name: income_tax_paid_4yrs
inputs.label_native: Total Income Tax & USC Paid over Last 4 Years (€)

calculators.formula_explanation:
1. Residential Stamp Duty: 1% on the first €1,000,000 of purchase price; 2% on the portion exceeding €1,000,000. (Note: Non-residential rate is 7.5%; bulk purchases of 10+ residential units incur 15%).
2. Central Bank Loan-to-Income (LTI) Limits: First Time Buyers (FTB) maximum mortgage = 4.0 × Gross Household Income. Second/Subsequent Buyers (SSB) maximum mortgage = 3.5 × Gross Household Income.
3. Minimum Deposit Requirement: FTB minimum deposit = 10% of purchase price. SSB minimum deposit = 10% of purchase price.
4. Help to Buy (HTB) Scheme (FTBs buying new builds ≤ €500,000): Refund of Income Tax and USC paid over prior 4 calendar years. Entitlement = Min(10% of property purchase price, €30,000, Total Income Tax/USC paid in 4 years).
5. First Home Scheme (FHS) Equity Support (New builds for FTBs): Provides equity contribution up to 30% of property purchase price (capped at 20% if HTB is also utilized).
6. Estimated Transaction Fees: Legal Conveyancing Fees (~€2,500-€3,500 + VAT) + Mortgage Valuation Fee (~€250) + Local Property Tax (LPT annual band estimate).
7. Net Out-of-Pocket Cash Required at Closing: Deposit Required (Purchase Price - Max Mortgage Loan - HTB Refund - FHS Equity) + Stamp Duty + Legal & Valuation Fees.

calculators.title_native: Irish Capital Acquisitions Tax (CAT) Gift & Inheritance Tax Calculator
calculators.title_en: Irish Capital Acquisitions Tax (CAT) Gift & Inheritance Tax Calculator
calculators.description_native: Calculate Capital Acquisitions Tax (CAT) on gifts and inheritances in Ireland, evaluating Group A/B/C lifetime tax-free thresholds, the €3,000 Annual Small Gift Exemption, Business/Agricultural Property Relief, and net CAT tax payable.

inputs.name: prior_taxable_benefits
inputs.label_native: Prior Taxable Benefits received in same Group since 5 Dec 1991 (€)

inputs.name: apply_small_gift_exemption
inputs.label_native: Apply Annual Small Gift Exemption (€3,000 per donor)

calculators.formula_explanation:
1. Valuation & Reliefs: If qualifying for Business Property Relief or Agricultural Relief, taxable market value is reduced by 90% (Taxable Benefit = Gross Value × 0.10).
2. Annual Small Gift Exemption: For lifetime gifts, €3,000 per donor per calendar year is deducted tax-free from taxable benefit value without reducing lifetime group thresholds.
3. Lifetime Tax-Free Group Thresholds: Group A (Child, or Parent taking absolute interest): €400,000; Group B (Sibling, Niece, Nephew, Grandchild, Lineal Ancestor/Descendant): €40,000; Group C (Stranger, Unrelated person, Non-married Cohabitant): €20,000.
4. Available Lifetime Group Threshold = Max(0, Statutory Group Threshold - Cumulative Prior Benefits received in same Group since 5 December 1991).
5. Taxable Excess = Max(0, Taxable Benefit - Available Lifetime Threshold).
6. Capital Acquisitions Tax (CAT) Payable = Taxable Excess × 33% (flat statutory CAT rate).
7. Statutory Filing Obligation: Revenue Form IT38 return must be filed online via ROS/MyAccount if total taxable benefit value reaches 80% or more of the applicable Group threshold.

calculators.title_native: Irish Proprietary Director Salary vs Dividend & Corporation Tax Calculator
calculators.title_en: Irish Proprietary Director Salary vs Dividend & Corporation Tax Calculator
calculators.description_native: Optimise profit extraction for proprietary directors of Irish Private Limited Companies (LTD), comparing salary, Executive PRSA pension contributions, dividends (subject to 25% DWT and marginal tax), 12.5% Corporation Tax, and Close Company Surcharges.

inputs.name: company_trading_profit
inputs.label_native: Company Annual Net Trading Profit before Remuneration (€)

inputs.name: small_benefit_voucher
inputs.label_native: Utilise Small Benefit Exemption (€1,000 voucher cap)

calculators.formula_explanation:
1. Corporate Tax Deductions: Director Salary, Company Pension Contributions (Executive PRSA), and Small Benefit Vouchers (up to €1,000 tax-free per year) are allowable business expenses reducing corporate taxable trading profit.
2. Corporation Tax (CT): 12.5% on Taxable Trading Profit. 25% CT on Non-Trading / Passive Investment Income.
3. Professional Services / Close Company Surcharge: Undistributed investment income or professional service income retained in company beyond 18 months incurs a 20% Close Company Surcharge.
4. Dividend Withholding Tax (DWT): 25% tax deducted at source by company upon dividend payout. Gross dividend is taxed in director's personal Form 11 return at marginal Income Tax (20%/40%) + USC (up to 11%) + Class S PRSI (4.1%), with credit given for 25% DWT prepaid.
5. Executive PRSA Pension Tax Advantage: Company contributions are 100% Corporation Tax deductible with no employer pension contribution limit under Irish Finance Act rules, creating 0% BIK for director.
6. Net Personal Value Comparison: Total Retained Wealth = (Director Net Take-Home Salary) + (Director Net Dividend) + (Executive Pension Wealth Accumulated) vs Total Corporate Tax & Personal Taxes Paid.
